items.note: Native-vector line chart, 19 paths, two series with circle markers over a grey boxed grid, y 0-140 by 20 against x 0.1 to 0.9, per-point data labels printed on the curves (14.6, 18.5, 25.2, 38.6, 76.7 on the lower series and 55, 60, 80, 120 on the upper one, the first of which is lost under the axis). Legend BELOW the plot inside the frame, two keys prefixed 't' and unreadable at 150 dpi. Three defects the crop exposes: a duplicate axis-number column (40, 20, 0) prints to the left of the real 0-140 column, which reads as a second y axis the geometry does not support; the caption sits 1.2 pt under the box, the tightest gap in the paper, and wraps to 'to realize electrification' immediately above the '8 Strengths and Weaknesses' heading, so caption welding steals a heading; and the two 213x66 and 213x58 pt bitmap patches layered inside this plot (recorded as excluded regions) make the figure measure as three boxes.

note:
**Coverage.** Twenty-five pages, twenty-nine measured regions on fourteen of them, all
accounted once: thirteen figure rows, two table rows and fourteen excluded regions. The
row count is BELOW the exhibit count for the first time in this run - twenty captioned
exhibits, fifteen rows - because the paper rasters its mathematics.

**This paper does not typeset its equations.** Every derivation from (5.1.2) onward is a
screenshot pasted into the flow. Fourteen of the twenty-nine measured regions are that
paste, including the two largest boxes in the whole document: the p5 parameters table at
34.72 per cent of its page and the p12 block at 34.71 per cent, which is SECTION 5.2.4
ITSELF - its own heading, its prose, its displays (5.2.7) and (5.2.8) - pasted whole. An
ink-ranked census would name that block the paper's second figure. It is the section.

**Six exhibits print no region.** Figures 3 and 4 are the paper's sharpest fault: p10
prints only the merged line 'Figure3: The primary site we choose     Figure4: The
development period network', twelve points under an equation paste, and the rest of the
page between that line and the 5.2.3 heading is blank - no artwork for either figure
anywhere. Two numbered exhibits are caption-only in this copy. Tables 3, 4, 5 and 6 are
the other four: all are three-band text blocks with heavy rules and zebra shading that
the region pass never clusters (p16, p17, p22), and p22's '22 paths, 0 regions' warning
is exactly that page's stacked Table 5 and Table 6.

**The numbering is one level off and the contents page lies.** The TOC prints '4 Model
Parameters / 5 Model Construction / 5.1.1 / 5.2.4 Commercial Model of Electric Vehicle
Charging Station / 5.2.5 The Competitive Exclusion Model', while the body prints '4 Model
Construction / 4.1 / 4.1.1 / 5.2.4 The Competitive Exclusion Model' - the whole 4.x and
5.x block shifted one level. Two section titles therefore exist ONLY inside bitmaps and
never in the text layer: '4 Model Parameters' (p5) and '5.2.4 Commercial Model of
Electric Vehicle Charging Station' (p12). The p5 table is filed under an unnumbered
heading for that reason.

**Merged caption lines.** p10, p15 and p16 each print TWO labels on ONE physical line
with no delimiter and no gap, so the caption-to-box join has to be made on the caption
fragment's x-range: p15's left fragment belongs to Figure 8 (Australia) and its right
fragment to Figure 9 (China), p16's left to Figure 10 (Uruguay) and right to Figure 11
(US). Any adjacency rule keyed on the line centre pairs both captions with one box.

**What the artwork is actually doing.** The four country scatters (Figures 8-11) are one
template: bare X/Y axes, red plus markers outside a black ellipse, blue dots inside, no
legend, no title, no shared scale - Australia is drawn 0-500 by 100-600 while China is
0-600 by 100-500, so the two cannot be compared by eye. The red/blue meaning is delivered
by the prose sentence under the caption ('The red cross in the figure is not in the 50%
circle, and the blue point have the opposite meaning') and the 50 per cent circle is
never labelled on any of the four. Figures 5 and 6 are the same MATLAB
competitive-exclusion template, curves self-labelled 'x1(t)' and 'x2(t)' in-panel with no
legend; Figure 6 adds four callout boxes whose X/Y pairs (13.03 / 2.734e+06, 16.07 /
8.202e+06, 18.43 / 1.367e+07, 55.15 / 2.734e+07) are what the prose quotes, so the chart
is doing the table's work. Its caption still reads 'Figure6: Data analysis of the figure
X.' - an unfilled placeholder - and its green reference line is lettered y=273390000
where Figure 5 letters the same line y=27339000, one zero apart, against its own callout
of 2.734e+07.

**Native vectors and their leaks.** Figures 13-15 are drawn as vectors (21, 26 and 19
drawing paths), so their axis numbers reach the text layer ahead of their caption lines -
p20's first caption token looks like an axis label to a text pass. Figure 13 prints a
regression annotation ('y = 0.0283x', 'R^2 = 1') as a drawn text box over five points;
Figure 14, on the same page and in the same claim, prints no annotation at all. Figure 15
is the only row measured as three regions: two bitmap patches (213x66 and 213x58 pt) were
embedded ON TOP of its own vector plot, at exactly the plot's data width, so the
measurer's three boxes are one chart with one legend, one axis set and one caption.

**Grid notes.** Table 1 is the only measured grid and the only decimal-aligned one
(right-aligned counts with thousands separators and two places, zebra on the Urban and
Rural rows, caption 17.4 pt above and its top rule 3 pt under the caption glyphs). The
four unmeasured grids, read one crop at a time: Table 3 is 12 rows by 4 columns at 438.6
pt with mixed precision and the country stub misspelt 'German'; Table 4 is 7 rows by 2
columns at 275.4 pt with visibly uneven columns; Table 5 is 5 by 2 at 181.9 pt set in
monospace Courier; Table 6 is 5 by 3 at 146.4 pt with subscripted headers and a
caption/ prose disagreement ('intrinsic' in the caption, 'inherent' in the text). None of
the four has a vertical rule; all four carry the same three heavy full-width strokes and
the same zebra banding.

**Apparatus limits worth keeping.** The Chinese resale watermark prints above six pages
and the layout pass reads it as `caption_above` on every raster that opens a page; on p10
it is overprinted by body text ('charging station near the nearest minute to recharge the
vehicle.' printed over 'Team # 80386 Page 7 of 21'). Table 3 alone spells its label
'Table 3:' with a space, against the glued 'FigureN:' everywhere else. The caption of
Figure 15 sits 1.2 pt under its box - welded - and wraps to 'to realize electrification'
immediately above the '8 Strengths and Weaknesses' heading, so caption welding steals a
heading on that page.


Excluded regions, one line each.

The crop's top edge also clips the prose lead-in line. No axes, no caption.
p6r2: A pasted EQUATION fragment at roughly 6 pt: four rewritten charging-pile formulas (5.1.5) to (5.1.8) with their italic lead-ins 'Considering that we have two kinds of charging piles, we can rewrite the formula (5.1.4) as:', 'Set as:' and 'According to the equation (5.1.7) we can get:' baked into the same bitmap. It occupies only the left 315 pt of the 455 pt measure, which is why its 252 pt box looks like a small figure; it is a typographic block. No axes, no caption.
p7r1: A 291x32 pt PROSE strip: 'Where r1 is the proportion of supercharging, r2 is the proportion of destination charging piles. Then we get:' plus the head of equation (5.1.9). The subscripts are inline images stripped from the text layer, so the page reads 'Where  is the proportion' to any text-only pass - the strip is exactly the seam where the paper's maths leaves the text layer. No axes, no caption.
p9r1: A 280x36 pt EQUATION fragment: 'Then we set up the decision variables as X_ij = { 1 / 0' with the brace left UNCLOSED and the true-branch condition missing, i.e. a truncated paste. Its width is just the length of that sentence, so it measures as a wide thin figure. No axes, no caption.
p9r2: A 453x234 pt paste that spans the WHOLE text measure and so swallows prose as well as maths: 'Then we can get:', the double-sum objective tagged (5.2.2), the sentence 'Our goal is to work out the formula and get the maximum.', the four-line system (5.2.3) under one large left brace, then 'Where:' and two bullets. Because the box equals the measure, its geometry is meaningless as a figure; the equation numbers hang at x~500 pt, INSIDE the box, which is how the capture was recognised. No axes, no caption.
p10r1: An EQUATION block, and the paper's worst exhibit fault. The box holds 'Based on the central ground theory, we can get:', r_m = V_car*t_f/lambda_s tagged (5.2.5), its three 'Where:' bullets, 'D_m can be calculated in the equation shown below:', D_m = 16*8*[alpha*mu_1 + (1-alpha)*mu_2] tagged (5.2.6) and the closing sentence 'almost 95.'. Twelve points under it, ONE printed line carries TWO caption labels - 'Figure3: The primary site we choose     Figure4: The development period network' - and NO artwork for either figure is printed anywhere on the page: the rest of p10 is blank between that line and the 5.2.3 heading. Two numbered exhibits are therefore caption-only in this copy, and a region-only census attaches both of them to an equation paste.
p12r1: A 445x391 pt page-fragment raster at 34.71 per cent of its page - a hundredth of a point behind the p5 parameters table, so the two largest boxes in the paper are both non-exhibits - and it is SECTION 5.2.4 PASTED WHOLE: its own heading '5.2.4 Commercial Model of Electric Vehicle Charging Station', the prose 'Due to the short range of electric vehicles and the lack of charging stations...', the displays (5.2.7) and (5.2.8) and their 'Where:' bullets. The heading is the finding: that section title appears in the table of contents and NOWHERE in the text layer, because it only exists inside this bitmap, and the body then prints '5.2.4 The Competitive Exclusion Model of Biological Groups' as the next heading - so the body's 5.2.4 is the contents' 5.2.5. rules: Twenty-nine measured regions on fourteen of twenty-five pages resolve to FIFTEEN exhibit rows - thirteen figures and two tables - plus fourteen excluded regions, and every region is claimed exactly once [place.doc_order].

This is the first paper in the run where the surplus runs the other way: twenty captioned exhibits, fifteen rows. Fourteen of the twenty-nine regions are pasted prose or equations, not artwork, because the authors set no mathematics in the typesetter - every derivation is a screenshot [geometry.family].

Six printed exhibits own no region and are recorded as declared gaps rather than invented rows: Figures 3 and 4 print one merged caption line with no artwork anywhere on p10, and Tables 3, 4, 5 and 6 are unruled or lightly-ruled text blocks the region pass never clusters [caption.verbatim].

Placement is one continuous run, not a per-section spread: eleven of fifteen rows fall inside 5.2 and 5.3, the South Korea application and the regional-difference discriminant, and the front half of the paper holds four [place.section_path].

Section kind is dominated by the two modelling stretches - four model rows, five solution rows - with two test rows, one symbol table, two rows in section 6's unclassified 'other' stretch and one sensitivity row [place.section_kind].

Rows sit high: six in the top third, five in the middle, four at the foot, and not one exhibit takes a page - the tallest is the p5 parameters table at 34.7 per cent, which is a symbol block, not a chart [place.page_zone].

Nothing is solo-page and nothing fills a page: the mean row covers 9.6 per cent of its page, and the four country scatters that carry the discriminant argument cover 5.3 to 5.8 per cent each [place.area_frac].

Caption side does not vary in this paper: all thirteen figures print their caption BELOW the box (gaps 1.2 to 10.2 pt) and both tables print ABOVE it (1.4 and 17.4 pt), so a single signed rule classifies the whole paper [caption.position].

Numbering is 'FigureN:' and 'TableN:' - label glued to the number with no space and a colon after it, no full stop - and the spelling is uniform across all fourteen quoted captions, unlike the two-way spelling the unmeasured Table 3 uses [caption.numbering].
Captions are bare noun phrases and stay short: seven words minimum, a median of seven, sixteen at the longest, one sentence each and never two [caption.words].

No caption carries a unit, none names a variable, none states a condition and none draws a conclusion - voice is `none` on all fourteen, so the caption never does interpretive work in this paper [caption.voice].

Captions are also semantically thin: they name the SUBJECT ('the population distribution of Australia') and never the reading, which is why every one of the four country plots needs a prose sentence under it to say what red and blue mean [caption.sentences].
Family mix is line-led and scatter-heavy: seven line rows, five scatter rows and one map - and the five scatters are all the same discriminant template at four different countries [geometry.family].

Legends are mostly absent: eight of thirteen figures carry none, three put a legend INSIDE the plot area (Figures 1, 2 and 12), one uses an outside-LEFT stepped stack (Figure 7's Gini bands) and one sits BELOW its frame (Figure 15) [geometry.legend].

No figure has a colourbar, including the world choropleth - Figure 7 keys its continuous-looking Gini scale as a DISCRETE eight-band legend with a 'No data' swatch, so a colourbar detector would report one and be wrong [geometry.colorbar].
Nothing is three-dimensional: no perspective bars, no surface mesh, no isometric axes anywhere in the thirteen figures [geometry.three_d].

Panels are not pasted here at all - panel_count is 1 on every row and no row is a panel of another - so the multi-box cases (Figures 3+4 sharing a caption line, and Figure 15's two bitmap patches) are handled as gaps and exclusions instead [geometry.panel_count].
Printed numbers are axis furniture in twelve of thirteen figures; Figure 7 is the single exception because a map has no axes to print on [geometry.printed_numbers].

Three figures label their data directly and they are the paper's numeric exhibits: Figures 5 and 6 print the in-panel curve names plus a green reference-line tag, and Figure 15 prints a value on every vertex [geometry.data_labels].

Both grids are horizontal-only 'booktabs' - a heavy rule under the header, a heavy foot, no vertical rule anywhere - and both carry no verticals even though every other paper in this stretch boxes its grids [table.rule_style].

Both grids are striped too: the p5 parameters table shades every second symbol row and Table 1 shades only its Urban and Rural rows, so this paper uses zebra as a default where the previous paper in the queue used none at all [table.zebra].
Grid size tracks content, not a template: eighteen symbol rows by three columns for the parameter list against four body rows by three for the measured result [table.rows].
Column count is three on both measured grids, but for different reasons - the parameters table's third column IS a unit column and Table 1's third column is a second count [table.cols].

Header treatment is uniform at one header row, and the parameters table's header (Symbol | Definition | Unit) exists only inside its raster, so no text-layer pass can read that grid at all [table.header_rows].

Units live in a real column here, not in the header: every p5 symbol row ends in 'miles', 'cars/h', 'hours' or '-', and Table 1 prints no unit of any kind because its caption carries the nouns [table.units_in_header].

Decimal alignment splits the two grids: Table 1 right-aligns its thousands-separated counts on a common two-place decimal, while the parameters table has no numeric column to align [table.decimal_aligned].

Widths differ by a factor of 1.16 - 425.2 pt full-measure for the parameters table against 365.6 pt half-measure for Table 1 - so width is a function of column count and not of importance [table.width].

No merged cell, no diagonal header anywhere, and no continued table: the four unmeasured tables on p16, p17 and p22 are separate grids stacked with about 7 pt between them, not one grid split by a page break [table.merged_cells].

Citation is degenerate - ONE numbered reference in the entire body ('From figure 1' on p8) and thirteen rows that are never named by number at all, so this paper cannot be read as a numbered sequence [mention.style].

That single numbered citation is also the only negative lead: Figure 1 prints on p7 and is named on p8, one page AFTER the chart, which is the reverse of every other paper in the census [mention.lead_pages].

Everything else refers demonstratively - 'the figure above', 'the table below', 'The result is shown in figure', 'Unbalanced country:' over the pair, 'Balanced Country：' over the next pair - so exhibit identity is carried by position and by the country header, never by the exhibit's own number [mention.lead_sentence].

Counts are one wherever they exist: no exhibit is named twice, and the two figures with no citation of any kind (Figures 14 and 15) are also the two that come after the paper stops referring to artwork at all [mention.count].

No row quotes a reading sentence after its caption: trail_sentence is empty on all fifteen rows, because this paper puts the interpretation BEFORE the figure and never after it [mention.trail_sentence].

Three columns - Symbol, Definition, Unit - over eighteen symbol rows from N to x2, with HORIZONTAL-ONLY rules (one rule under the header, one at the foot, none above the header) and no vertical rules at all, so the style is `booktabs`; it is also the ONLY grid in the paper with alternating row shading, a light grey zebra band on every second row.
